# User guide: The terminal

## In plain words

Each workspace shows its agent in a terminal inside the Unraid page. The terminal does more than show text. A file name that an agent prints is a link that opens the file. A web address is a link too. You can copy text out of the terminal and paste text into it, on a desktop and on a phone. You can drag files onto the terminal, or paste a picture, and the plugin saves them in the workspace folder so that the agent can read them. On a phone, a row of keys under the terminal gives you Esc, Tab and the arrow keys. This page explains each of these, and the two settings that change how the terminal looks.

Words used on this page:

- **Terminal**: the text window that shows the agent. It runs on the server, so it keeps running when you close the browser tab.
- **Workspace folder**: the folder that you chose when you made the workspace. The agent works in this folder.
- **Drawer**: the panel on the side of the page that lists your workspaces.
- **Pull tab**: the small strip of icons at the edge of the closed drawer.

## Where to find it

- **The terminal page**: the **AI CLI Agents** tab of Unraid. Each open workspace has its own terminal.
- **Paste and Copy icons**: in the drawer. When the drawer is pinned open, a row of icons shows at the top of the drawer. When the drawer is not pinned, the same icons sit on the pull tab. On a phone, the pull tab is short. Tap the "more" icon (three dots) on the pull tab to show the rest of the icons.
- **Upload**: the **Upload file** item in a workspace's "..." menu in the drawer, or drag a file onto the page.
- **Key row**: under the terminal, on a phone or a tablet only.
- **Colour scheme and Text size**: **Settings, Configuration** tab.
- **Largest upload**: **Settings, Configuration** tab.

## How to use it

### Open a file from a link in the terminal

When an agent prints a file path, the terminal makes it a link. Point at the path to see the underline.

1. Click the path.
2. Expect: a text file opens in an editor window on top of the terminal. The window has a **Save** button, a button that copies the file contents, and a button that copies a bookmark link to the file. A Markdown file also has **Edit**, **Split** and **Preview** buttons.
3. Press the close button (**X**) to go back to the terminal. If you changed the file, the plugin asks you before it closes the window.

A file that is not a text file opens in the file browser of Unraid, in a new tab.

A path becomes a link only when the file exists. The terminal asks the server when you point at a line, and it underlines only the paths that are real files. The underline can show a fraction of a second after the pointer arrives. A path with a typo, a file that is gone, a folder, and a place that the plugin does not open (for example, under `/etc`) get no underline. The plugin remembers each answer for a few seconds, so a file that an agent creates becomes a link soon after.

A path that starts with `./` or `/` or `~/` can be any file type, for example `~/bin/backup`. A path from the workspace folder, such as `docs/specs/plan.md`, needs a known text-file ending (md, txt, php, json, yml, sh, log, conf, py and others). A bare file name, such as `README.md`, is a link when that file is in the workspace folder. A word that only looks like a file name (for example `e.g`) is not a link. If the check cannot reach the server, a path with a known ending or a start of `./`, `/` or `~/` and a file type still links, and the other kinds do not. Web addresses, the plugin's own pages and Notebook references are links at once and are not checked. A path that the agent's screen breaks over two lines is still one link.

A relative path is read from the workspace folder. If you open a path in another way (for example, from a Notebook note) and the file is not there, a small message says "File not found" and shows the path. If the file is in a place that the plugin does not open, the message says that the location cannot be opened from here.

> [!NOTE]
> The plugin gives each agent a short instruction that asks it to write a path that the terminal can use. A file inside the workspace is written as a path from the workspace folder, and a file in the workspace root starts with `./`. A file in another place is written with its full path. If one agent writes a bare file name, ask it to write the path.

### Open a web address or a Notebook note

1. Click a web address (a name that starts with http:// or https://).
2. Expect: the address opens in a new browser tab.

A link to one of the plugin's own pages (for example, a link to the file viewer of this page) opens in the tab that you already use. It does not open a second copy of the terminal. The plugin makes only these two kinds of text into links: web addresses and the plugin's own pages. No other kind of text is a link.

A reference to a Notebook note that an agent prints (it looks like `artefact:a_` followed by twelve letters and digits) is a link as well. Click it, and the Notebook drawer opens on that note. See [The Notebook](notebook.md).

### Copy text out of the terminal

There are three ways to copy.

**1. The agent copies for you.** Some agents have a copy command. When the agent uses it, the text goes to your clipboard and a small message says "Copied to clipboard".

If the browser blocks the write (this happens on a page that uses plain HTTP and not HTTPS), a box opens with the text already selected. The box is called **Copy Manually**. Press Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on a Mac) and close the box.

**2. Drag with Shift held down (desktop).** The terminal uses the mouse for the agent's own menus, so a plain drag does not select text. Hold **Shift** while you drag. The browser then selects the text itself. A small hint at the bottom of the terminal says "Shift+drag to copy". Press the small **x** in the hint to hide it for good. The browser remembers this choice.

**3. The Copy icon in the drawer (all devices).**

1. Press the **Copy from terminal** icon (two sheets of paper).
2. Expect: a full-screen window called **Select text** opens. It shows up to 2000 lines of the workspace history as plain text. It opens at the newest line.
3. Select the part that you want. On a touch screen, touch and hold a word, then drag the handles. On a desktop, drag with the mouse.
4. Press **Copy selection**. Or press **Copy all** to copy everything.
5. Expect: the window says "Copied" and the number of characters.
6. Press **Done**.

If you press **Copy selection** with nothing selected, the window says "Select some text first". If the plugin cannot read the history, the window shows the text that is on the screen now.

### Paste text into the terminal

Normal paste works in the terminal: press Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on a Mac) while the terminal has focus. The paste icon of the drawer does the same without the keyboard.

1. Copy the text somewhere.
2. Press the **Paste to terminal** icon (a clipboard) in the drawer.
3. Expect: the text goes into the agent's input, and a small message says "Pasted into terminal". The focus returns to the terminal, so you can keep typing.

If the browser does not let the page read your clipboard, a box opens. It is called **Paste into Terminal**. The box says that the browser blocked direct clipboard access, which needs HTTPS.

1. Paste your text into the box. Use Ctrl+V or Cmd+V. On a phone, touch and hold in the box and choose **Paste**.
2. Press **Send**.
3. Expect: the text goes to the agent, and the box closes.

Limits on a paste:

- A paste that has more than five lines asks first: "Paste N lines into the terminal?" Press **OK** to go on. A long paste into an agent's input can start many actions, so the question is a safety check.
- A paste can hold at most 256 KB. A larger paste is refused with the message "Paste too large (max 256 KB)".
- An empty clipboard gives the message "Clipboard is empty".

The text of a paste goes only to the agent's terminal. The plugin does not write it to the log.

### Upload files to the workspace

You can give a file to an agent by uploading it. The plugin saves the file in the workspace folder.

**Drag files onto the page.**

1. Drag one or more files from your computer over the terminal.
2. Expect: the **Upload to Workspace** window opens at once and stays open while you drag. It shows the folder that will receive the files.
3. Drop the files in the window. Or click the drop area and pick files. You can pick several files at once.
4. Expect: a list shows each file with its size. An image shows a small thumbnail. If you gave only one file, a name field lets you change its name.
5. To take a file out of the list, press the small red **x** at the end of its row.
6. Press **Confirm Upload**.
7. Expect: a bar shows the progress, and a line shows "1 of 3" and the file name. When all files are saved, a message says "File path copied to clipboard" and shows the saved path or paths. The message closes after three seconds. You can press **OK** to close it sooner.

Press **Cancel** at any time before the upload ends to close the window without a save.

**From the drawer menu.** Open the "..." menu of a workspace and choose **Upload file**. The same window opens. The files go to that workspace, also when it is not the one that you look at.

**Paste a picture.** Copy a picture (for example, a screenshot) and paste it into the terminal with Ctrl+V or Cmd+V. You can also use the **Paste to terminal** icon in the drawer.

1. Expect: no window opens. The plugin saves the picture in the workspace folder with a name such as `pasted_image_2026-10-12T09-30-00.png`. The time is in the name, so a new picture never replaces an older one.
2. Expect: the saved path is typed into the agent's input, with a space after it. The agent reads the picture from that path.
3. Expect: a small preview of the picture shows at the top right of the terminal for about four seconds. Click or tap it to see it full size. Close it with the small round **x**, with a tap outside the picture, or with a swipe.

The agent gets a path and not a picture. It cannot show its own "[Image]" marker, because that marker comes from a clipboard read that a server without a screen cannot do. Most agents open the picture from the path with no more help.

A file that is not a picture, when you paste it, opens the upload window. After the upload, the saved path is typed into the agent's input. If you pasted several files, the paths go in one line. A path that has a space in it is put between quote marks.

**Where the file lands.**

- Every upload goes to the workspace that you have open. The plugin never uses a fixed folder. If no workspace is open, a message says "No workspace open" and asks you to open one first.
- The upload from the drawer menu is the one exception: it goes to the workspace of that menu, for that one upload.
- The name of the file keeps its letters, but the plugin removes any folder part and any control characters from it.
- A file with the same name as a file that is already in the folder replaces that file. Change the name in the name field if you want to keep both.
- After an upload that is not a paste, the plugin copies the saved path to your clipboard (one path on each line if you sent several files). Paste it into the agent's input.

**Large files.** The plugin sends a big file in small pieces, one after the other, and it tries a piece again once if the network fails. The progress bar covers all files together. A big file works on a slow link.

**Size limit.** The **Largest upload** setting is the largest file the window accepts. The default is 512 MB. Set it to 0 for no limit. A file over the limit is refused with a message that gives the file size and the limit. An empty file (0 bytes) is refused as well.

If one file fails, the files before it stay saved, and the window keeps the failed file and the files after it in the list. Fix the problem (or take the bad file out of the list) and press **Confirm Upload** again.

### Use the terminal on a phone or a tablet

A touch screen has no Shift key, no mouse wheel and often no Esc key. The terminal adds controls for these.

- **Key row.** A row under the terminal has **Esc**, **Tab**, **^C** (the stop command), and the four arrow keys. It also has **Paste** and **Select**. On a narrow phone, **Paste** and **Select** show only their icons. A key keeps the phone keyboard open, because pressing a key does not move focus.
- **Swipe.** Swipe up or down with one finger on the terminal to scroll the history of the session. A swipe down shows older lines. The page does not scroll or reload while you swipe.
- **Latest.** While you look at history, a **Latest** button shows at the right. Press it, or tap the terminal, to go back to the live screen. If you type a key while you look at history, the terminal first goes back to the live screen and then sends the key. **Esc** only closes the history and does not reach the agent.
- **Touch and hold.** Touch and hold the terminal without moving. A small menu shows at your finger with **Paste** and **Select**. **Paste** acts like the **Paste to terminal** icon. **Select** opens the **Select text** window that is described above.
- **Hint.** On first use, a hint says "Swipe to scroll history · hold for Paste / Select". Press the **x** to hide it for good.
- **Keyboard.** When the phone keyboard opens, the terminal and the key row get smaller so that both stay in view.
- **Upload.** The upload window fills the screen. Its buttons are large enough to touch.

On a phone, the voice microphone bar sits above the key row while you dictate. See [Voice](voice.md).

### Switch quickly between workspaces

A terminal that you did not open takes a moment to connect. To remove this wait, the page on a desktop keeps a hidden, live terminal for each running workspace, up to ten. It starts with the workspace on screen and then the ones you used last. When you click a running workspace, its terminal shows at once.

A phone or a tablet does not do this. It connects a terminal only when you open it. The page also does this only while you are at the page (it is visible, and you used the mouse or keyboard in the last ten minutes).

## Choices and settings

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Colour scheme** (Configuration tab) | The colors of the terminal windows. Choices: **Dark** (white text on a dark gray ground), **Light** (dark text on white), **Solarized** (muted blue-gray text on a dark teal ground). | Dark | When the dark ground is hard to read in your room, or you use a light Unraid theme and want the terminal to match. |
| **Text size** (Configuration tab) | The text size of the terminal windows, in pixels. Allowed values: 8 to 32. | 14 | When the text is too small on your screen, or you want more lines on the screen. |
| **Largest upload** (Configuration tab) | The largest file that the upload window accepts, in MB. 0 means no limit. | 512 | When you need to send a larger file, or you want to protect the server's disk from large files. |
| **Keep typing fast when the server is busy** (Configuration tab) | Gives the Unraid web page and the terminals a higher priority than other programs, and the plugin background work a lower one. Docker containers, virtual machines and array services are not changed. | Off | When typing in a terminal lags while the server is busy. |
| **Agent temporary files** (Configuration tab) | Where agents keep their temporary files. RAM is the default. A folder on a pool keeps large temporary files out of memory, so typing stays quick. | RAM | When agent temporary files grow large. |

**Keep typing fast when the server is busy** applies at once. Choose **On**, and typing in a terminal stays quick when Plex, a virtual machine or a backup uses the processor. Your agents keep the normal priority, so the setting does not slow them down. Choose **Off** to put every program back at its normal priority.

A change to **Colour scheme** or **Text size** reaches a terminal window when that window loads. Reload the terminal page to see the change in the windows that are already open.

The Paste and Copy icons, the hint and the key row have no setting. They show when they apply. When **Let agents manage the plugin** is on, an agent can also change the theme and the font size for you. See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md).

### How the page fits your Unraid theme

Unraid has two kinds of theme. The **white** and **black** themes put the menu in a bar above the page. The **gray** and **azure** themes put the menu in a narrow bar down the left edge of the window. The plugin finds out which kind you use and keeps its terminal, drawer, pull tab and pop-up messages clear of that bar. The bar stays on a phone as well, so the plugin leaves room for it on a phone.

The plugin's buttons use the look of Unraid's own buttons (a light ground, a thin border, normal capital letters) in all four themes. You do not need to set anything.

## What happens behind the scenes

The terminal is a web page for one tmux session (tmux is the session manager that keeps the agent running on the server). The plugin adds the clickable links, the copy and paste bridge, and the touch controls to that page. An upload goes to the server in small pieces and is put together there. See C4 Component: React Terminal Spa and C4 Component: Server Rendered Ui.

When the plugin types a fixed notice into an agent (for example, a Relay notice), it presses Enter and then looks at the screen. While the notice is still in the input line, it presses Enter again after a short wait, up to a few times. You do not need to do anything. See [Agent Relay](relay.md).

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| A file name in the terminal is not a link. | The file does not exist (check for a typo), it is in a place that the plugin does not open, or the name is not in the workspace folder. | Check the path. Ask the agent to write the path from the workspace folder, for example `./notes.txt`. |
| The message "File not found" shows when you click a link. | The path does not point to a file now. The agent may have named a wrong or removed file. | Check the path. Ask the agent for the right one. |
| The message "That location cannot be opened from here" shows. | The path is outside the places that the plugin opens. | Open the file with the Unraid file browser or another tool. |
| A plain drag does not select text. | The terminal uses the mouse for the agent. | Hold Shift while you drag, or use the **Copy from terminal** icon. |
| The **Paste into Terminal** box opens each time. | The page runs on plain HTTP, or the browser blocks clipboard reads. | Use the box. Or open the Unraid page with HTTPS. |
| "Paste too large (max 256 KB)". | The paste is above the limit. | Save the text in a file and upload the file. |
| The upload window does not open when you drag. | No workspace is open. | Open a workspace, then drag again. |
| "Upload Failed" with a file name and a size. | The file is over the **Largest upload**, or it is empty. | Raise the limit in **Settings, Configuration**, or choose a different file. |
| "Upload Failed" with a network message. | The network dropped during the upload. The plugin already tried each piece twice. | Press **Confirm Upload** again. The files that were saved stay saved. |
| A pasted picture shows no preview. | The picture could not be read, or the page blocked the preview. The upload may still have worked. | Look in the workspace folder for a file that starts with `pasted_image_`. |
| The key row does not show on a tablet. | The browser does not report a touch screen. | Use the drawer icons and the **Select** window on that device. |
| A terminal window uses the old color or text size after you change a setting. | The window reads the setting when it loads. | Reload the terminal page. |
